topics.name: 2-Step vs Agentic vs Hybrid RAG
topics.description: Comparing the three RAG architectures and when to use each.
notes: ## 三种 RAG 架构
- 2-Step RAG：检索总是在生成之前执行，流程简单、可预测，适合 FAQ、文档问答。
- Agentic RAG：由 LLM 驱动的 agent 在推理过程中决定『何时』以及『如何』检索。
- Hybrid RAG：兼具两者特点，加入查询预处理、检索验证和生成后检查。
## 官方对比表
- 2-Step：控制力高、灵活性低、延迟快。
- Agentic：控制力低、灵活性高、延迟可变。
- Hybrid：控制力与灵活性居中，延迟可变。
## Agentic RAG 的最小条件
- agent 只需要能访问一个或多个可获取外部知识的工具（文档加载器、Web API、数据库查询等）。
- 已有知识库（SQL 数据库、CRM、内部文档系统）无需重建，可作为工具接入 Agentic RAG。
## Hybrid RAG 的三个组件
- Query enhancement：改写不清晰的问题、生成多个变体或补充上下文。
- Retrieval validation：判断检索结果是否相关且足够，不够则优化查询再检索。
- Answer validation：检查答案的准确性、完整性以及与来源的一致性，必要时重新生成或修订。
## 延迟与评估
- 2-Step 的 LLM 调用次数上限已知，延迟更可预测（前提是 LLM 推理耗时占主导）。
- 检索 API、网络、数据库查询的耗时仍可能让真实延迟波动。
- 官方教程『Agentic RAG with Self-Correction』被归类为 Hybrid RAG 的示例。
- 评估检索质量可参考 LangSmith 的 RAG 评估教程（正确性、相关性、groundedness、retrieval quality）。

topics.name: Agentic RAG Graph in LangGraph
topics.description: Nodes, edges and loop control in the custom LangGraph RAG agent.
notes: ## LangGraph 自定义 Agentic RAG 图
- State 使用 MessagesState；节点读取状态并返回状态更新，而不是直接修改状态。
- 节点：generate_query_or_respond、retrieve（ToolNode）、rewrite_question、generate_answer。
- grade_documents 是挂在 retrieve 之后的条件边路由函数，返回下一个节点名。
```python
def generate_query_or_respond(state: MessagesState):
response = response_model.bind_tools([retriever_tool]).invoke(state["messages"])
return {"messages": [response]}
## 组装流程
- START → generate_query_or_respond；有 tool_calls 则进入 retrieve，否则 END 直接回复。
- retrieve → grade_documents：相关 → generate_answer；不相关 → rewrite_question。
- rewrite_question → generate_query_or_respond，让 agent 重新检索。
- generate_answer → END。
```python
workflow.add_node("retrieve", ToolNode([retriever_tool]))
workflow.add_conditional_edges("retrieve", grade_documents)
workflow.add_edge("rewrite_question", "generate_query_or_respond")
## 细节
- 原始问题取 state["messages"][0]，检索内容取 state["messages"][-1]（ToolMessage）。
- 循环需要终止条件：条件边路由到 END，或设置 recursion_limit（超限抛 GraphRecursionError）。
- 可用 RemainingSteps 在步数不足时提前 END，返回当前状态而不报错。

topics.name: Retrievers, Vector Stores and Context
topics.description: Building retrieval tools and keeping retrieved context under control.
notes: ## 为 Agent 准备检索
- 流水线：Document loader → 切分 chunk → embedding → vector store → retriever。
- Document 有 page_content、metadata 和可选的 id；metadata 可记录来源等信息。
- Text splitter 把大文档切成可单独检索、且能放进上下文窗口的小块；RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter 是通用文本的推荐选择。
- add_start_index=True 会在 metadata 中保留 start_index（字符偏移）。
## VectorStore 与 Retriever
- VectorStore 不是 Runnable；Retriever 是 Runnable，支持 invoke / batch 及异步版本。
- vector_store.as_retriever(search_type=..., search_kwargs=...) 返回 VectorStoreRetriever。
- search_type：similarity（默认）、mmr、similarity_score_threshold。
```python
retriever = vector_store.as_retriever(
search_type="similarity",
search_kwargs={"k": 1},
## 检索工具与上下文
- 教程用 @tool 包装检索，docstring 即工具描述；索引只建一次（如 lru_cache 或启动时），不要每次调用都重建。
- 超长输入占用上下文，模型也可能在其中找不到信息，所以只检索相关片段。
- Deep Agents 教程把检索块写入文件系统、只返回路径，让子 agent 阅读并总结，保持主上下文干净。
## 安全
- 检索内容与系统提示共享上下文窗口，存在间接 prompt injection 风险；没有任何提示或分隔符方案能完全防止，需校验输出。

topics.name: SQL Agent as a Knowledge Source
topics.description: Using a database as retrieval source with guarded SQL tools.
notes: ## 其他知识源：SQL Agent
- 数据库也可以作为检索来源：把查询能力封装成工具交给 agent。
- 流程：获取表与 schema → 判断相关表 → 获取相关表 schema → 生成查询 → 用 LLM 复查常见错误 → 执行 → 根据数据库报错修正 → 生成回答。
- 工具：sql_db_list_tables、sql_db_schema、sql_db_query、sql_db_query_checker。
- 查询出错时，错误信息作为工具结果返回给模型，模型据此重写查询。
## 安全与约束
- 执行模型生成的 SQL 有固有风险：数据库权限应尽量收窄；教程中的工具仅为演示，不适用于生产。
- 系统提示约束：只查必要的列、默认用 top_k 限制结果数量、禁止 DML（INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DROP）。
- HumanInTheLoopMiddleware(interrupt_on={"sql_db_query": True}) 可在执行前暂停审核，需要 checkpointer 才能暂停与恢复。
## 自定义 LangGraph 版本
- 专用节点：list_tables、call_get_schema、get_schema、generate_query、check_query、run_query。
- 目的：可以强制工具调用并为每一步定制 prompt；预置 agent 只能靠系统提示约束行为。
```python
llm = model.bind_tools([get_schema_tool], tool_choice="any")
- generate_query 之后用条件边：有 tool_calls 去 check_query，否则 END。

questions.title: In 2-Step RAG, when does the retrieval step run?

options.text: Only when the model decides to call a tool
Always, before the generation step
After the answer has been generated
Only if a grader marks the question as complex

questions.explanation: In 2-Step RAG retrieval is always executed before generation, which makes the flow simple and predictable. Letting the model decide when to retrieve is what agentic RAG adds.

questions.title: According to the retrieval docs, what does an agent need in order to enable RAG behavior?

options.text: A fine-tuned embedding model
A graph with a grading node
Access to one or more tools that can fetch external knowledge
A persistent checkpointer

questions.explanation: The docs say the only requirement is tools that can fetch external knowledge, such as documentation loaders, web APIs or database queries. Grading nodes and checkpointers are optional additions.

questions.title: Which RAG architecture combines traits of 2-Step and Agentic RAG by adding query preprocessing, retrieval validation and post-generation checks?

options.text: Hybrid RAG
2-Step RAG
Agentic RAG with no validation
Keyword-only search

questions.explanation: Hybrid RAG introduces intermediate steps around retrieval and generation while keeping more control than a fully agentic design. 2-Step RAG has no such checks.

questions.title: Which tool does the docs' RAG evaluation tutorial use to measure answer correctness, relevance, groundedness and retrieval quality?

options.text: ToolNode
InMemoryVectorStore
RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
LangSmith

questions.explanation: The retrieval docs link a tutorial that evaluates a retrieve-then-generate app with LangSmith. The other options are building blocks of the app, not evaluators.

questions.title: Which are typical components of Hybrid RAG according to the docs?

options.text: Query enhancement
Retrieval validation
Answer validation
A single fixed retrieval with no checks

questions.explanation: Hybrid RAG adds query enhancement, retrieval validation and answer validation, often iterating between them. A fixed single retrieval with no checks describes a plain 2-Step pipeline.

questions.title: Why is latency generally more predictable in 2-Step RAG than in Agentic RAG?

options.text: It never calls an external retriever
Embeddings are cached automatically
The maximum number of LLM calls is known and capped
It streams tokens faster than agents

questions.explanation: A fixed pipeline has a known, capped number of LLM calls. The docs add that retrieval API and network delays can still make real latency vary.

questions.title: A team already stores its knowledge in a SQL database and a CRM. How do the retrieval docs suggest using it in Agentic RAG?

options.text: Re-embed everything into a new vector store first
Connect it as a tool for the agent
Export it to PDF and use only a document loader
Fine-tune the model on the data

questions.explanation: An existing knowledge base does not need rebuilding; it can be exposed as a tool for the agent. Alternatively it can be queried and its results passed as context in 2-Step RAG.

questions.title: How do the retrieval docs classify the LangGraph tutorial 'Agentic RAG with Self-Correction'?

options.text: 2-Step RAG, since retrieval is always executed first
A pure agentic RAG with no validation steps
A SQL agent example
Hybrid RAG, combining agentic reasoning with retrieval and self-correction

questions.explanation: The docs call it an example of Hybrid RAG: the model decides whether to retrieve (agentic) and a grade-and-rewrite loop validates retrieval. It is not a fixed 2-Step pipeline.

questions.title: Fill in the method that gives the model access to the retriever tool so it can choose between answering and retrieving.

options.text: with_tools
add_tool
bind_tools
register_tools

questions.explanation: bind_tools attaches the retriever tool to the model, which then either replies directly or emits a tool call. The other names are not the method the tutorial uses.

questions.title: The user says 'hello!' and the model replies without any tool call. What happens next in this graph?

options.text: retrieve runs with an empty query
The graph ends and the reply is returned to the user
grade_documents runs on the reply
rewrite_question runs

questions.explanation: Without tool_calls the router returns END, so the model's direct answer is the final result. Retrieval only runs when the model requests the retriever tool.

questions.title: This code runs right after the retrieve node. What does `context` contain?
questions.codeSnippet:
def grade_documents(state: MessagesState):
    question = state["messages"][0].content
    context = state["messages"][-1].content
    prompt = GRADE_PROMPT.format(question=question, context=context)
    ...

options.text: The original user question
The content of the tool message produced by retrieve
The rewritten question
The system prompt

questions.explanation: After retrieve (a ToolNode) the last message is the tool message holding the retrieved text, while the first message is the user's question. The grader compares the two.

questions.title: Complete the edge so that a rewritten question lets the agent attempt retrieval again.

options.text: retrieve
generate_answer
generate_query_or_respond
grade_documents

questions.explanation: The tutorial sends control back to generate_query_or_respond so the model can issue a new retriever tool call. retrieve is a ToolNode that runs tool calls requested by the model.

questions.title: Which statements describe the tutorial's rewrite_question node?

options.text: It reads the original question from state["messages"][0]
It asks the model for an improved question and returns it as a HumanMessage
It calls the retriever tool directly with the new query
It routes straight to generate_answer

questions.explanation: The node formats REWRITE_PROMPT with the first message and returns the model's improved question as a HumanMessage. Retrieval happens afterwards when control returns to generate_query_or_respond.

questions.title: The rewritten question never shows up in the graph state. What is wrong?
questions.codeSnippet:
def rewrite_question(state: MessagesState):
    question = state["messages"][0].content
    prompt = REWRITE_PROMPT.format(question=question)
    response = response_model.invoke([{"role": "user", "content": prompt}])
    state["messages"].append(HumanMessage(content=response.content))

options.text: REWRITE_PROMPT must be passed as a list
The node mutates the state and returns nothing; it should return {"messages": [HumanMessage(...)]}
invoke must be replaced with ainvoke
A HumanMessage cannot be used for a rewritten question

questions.explanation: LangGraph nodes should return state updates rather than mutate state. Returning the new message lets the reducer add it to messages.

questions.title: In this a/b loop, what does the RemainingSteps check achieve compared with having no such check?
questions.codeSnippet:
class State(TypedDict):
    aggregate: Annotated[list, operator.add]
    remaining_steps: RemainingSteps

def route(state: State) -> Literal["b", END]:
    if state["remaining_steps"] <= 2:
        return END
    return "b"

builder.add_conditional_edges("a", route)
builder.add_edge("b", "a")
graph = builder.compile()
result = graph.invoke({"aggregate": []}, {"recursion_limit": 4})

options.text: It raises GraphRecursionError earlier
It raises the recursion limit automatically
It disables the loop entirely
It ends the run with the accumulated state instead of raising GraphRecursionError

questions.explanation: RemainingSteps tracks the steps left before the recursion limit, so the router can route to END and return the current state. Without it the run raises GraphRecursionError.

questions.title: After grading marks the retrieved text as irrelevant, this node produces a nonsensical 'improved question'. Why?

options.text: state["messages"][-1] is the tool message with retrieved text, not the user's question; the tutorial reads index 0
A node cannot return a HumanMessage
REWRITE_PROMPT requires structured output
response_model must be bound to the retriever tool

questions.explanation: At this point in the graph the last message is the retrieved context, so the model rewrites document text instead of the question. The tutorial takes the question from messages[0] and the context from messages[-1].

questions.title: Which attributes does a LangChain Document have?

options.text: text, vector and score
page_content, metadata and an optional id
content, embedding and source_url
body, tags and chunk_size

questions.explanation: A Document holds page_content (the text), a metadata dict and an optional id string. Embeddings and scores are not Document attributes.

questions.title: Why are large documents split into chunks before indexing?

options.text: So embeddings are no longer needed
So the vector store can skip similarity search
So metadata can be discarded
So each chunk is retrievable individually and fits within a model's context window

questions.explanation: Text splitters break large documents into smaller pieces that can be retrieved on their own and fit in the context window. Splitting does not replace embeddings or similarity search.

questions.title: What does `docs` contain after this call?
questions.codeSnippet:
retriever = vector_store.as_retriever(
    search_type="similarity",
    search_kwargs={"k": 1},
)
docs = retriever.invoke("When was Nike incorporated?")

options.text: A list holding the single most similar Document
A single string with the best passage
Every chunk above a score threshold
The VectorStore object itself

questions.explanation: search_kwargs is passed to the underlying similarity search, so k=1 returns one Document in a list. A score threshold needs search_type similarity_score_threshold.

questions.title: Which search_type values does VectorStoreRetriever support?

options.text: similarity
mmr
similarity_score_threshold
keyword_only

questions.explanation: The supported types are similarity (default), mmr for maximum marginal relevance, and similarity_score_threshold to filter by score. keyword_only is not one of them.

questions.title: According to the Deep Agents RAG tutorial, why split documents into chunks before embedding?

options.text: Large chunks are harder to search over
Large chunks may not fit the model's finite context window or may use more tokens than necessary
Splitting removes the need for an embeddings model
Models can struggle to find information in very long inputs even when they fit

questions.explanation: The tutorial lists search difficulty, context-window and token cost, and weak recall over long inputs as reasons. Chunks still need embeddings for similarity search.

questions.title: Every call to this retriever tool is slow and costly. What is the most likely problem?

options.text: The index is rebuilt, re-embedding every chunk, on each call; build it once and reuse it
as_retriever cannot be used inside a tool
The docstring is too short to be a tool description
The chunks must be joined with a single newline

questions.explanation: The tutorial builds the retriever once in a helper cached with lru_cache(maxsize=1) and the tool only queries it. Rebuilding the vector store per call repeats all embedding work.

questions.title: Which statement about indirect prompt injection in RAG matches the Deep Agents tutorial?

options.text: Wrapping chunks in delimiters fully prevents it
It only affects remotely hosted vector stores
Retrieved chunks share the context window with the system prompt, and no prompt or delimiter strategy fully prevents the model from following embedded instructions
Setting temperature to 0 eliminates it

questions.explanation: Retrieved text sits beside the system prompt, so embedded instructions can be followed. Treat-as-data prompts help in some cases but are not reliable; validate outputs before surfacing them.

questions.title: In the Deep Agents RAG tutorial, why does the search tool write retrieved chunks to the agent filesystem and return only file paths?

options.text: The vector store cannot return text
ToolNode requires file paths as output
It lets later queries skip embedding
The orchestrator avoids holding full chunk text in its context while subagents read and summarize each file

questions.explanation: Returning paths keeps the orchestrator's context small, and chunk-analyst subagents read and summarize individual files. The tool still gets chunk text from the vector store.

questions.title: What do the SQL agent tutorials warn you to do about the database connection the agent uses?

options.text: Use admin credentials so queries never fail
Scope its permissions as narrowly as possible for the agent's needs
Share it with other applications
Disable the query tool

questions.explanation: Running model-generated SQL has inherent risks, and narrow permissions mitigate but do not eliminate them. Broad credentials make mistakes more damaging.

questions.title: Which steps does the LangChain SQL agent perform at a high level?

options.text: Fetch the available tables and schemas, then decide which tables are relevant
Double-check the generated query for common mistakes using an LLM
Execute the query and correct mistakes surfaced by the database engine until it succeeds
Embed the question and run vector similarity search over table rows

questions.explanation: The agent inspects tables and schemas, generates and checks a query, runs it, and retries on database errors. It queries via SQL tools, not via vector similarity.

questions.title: Which tool_choice value forces the model to emit a tool call in this dedicated node?

options.text: all
force
any
always

questions.explanation: The tutorial notes LangChain enforces that all models accept tool_choice="any" or a tool name. The other strings are not values the docs describe.

questions.title: Why does the custom LangGraph SQL agent use dedicated nodes (list tables, get schema, generate query, check query) instead of relying on the prebuilt agent's system prompt?

options.text: Prebuilt agents cannot call SQL tools
The Graph API requires one node per table
Dedicated nodes let you force tool calls when needed and customize the prompt for each step
Dedicated nodes remove the need for a model

questions.explanation: The prebuilt agent is constrained only by its system prompt. Dedicated nodes give stricter control by forcing tool calls and tailoring each step's prompt.
